headline: Govt orders Army deployment in 6 districts over banned AL anniversary
summary: Troops will be stationed in Dhaka, Gazipur, Narayanganj, Faridpur, Gopalganj, and Chattogram for one week to maintain law and order.
details: The government has decided to deploy the Army across six districts to maintain law and order surrounding the founding anniversary of the Awami League, whose activities are currently banned.
The chosen areas for initial deployment include Dhaka, Gazipur, Narayanganj, Faridpur, Gopalganj, and Chattogram.
The troops will operate under the "In Aid to Civil Power" mandate for one week to keep the situation stable and support other law-enforcing agencies.
This move comes ahead of the June 23 anniversary events, where the government aims to prevent potential unrest.
caption:
Army troops are being deployed to 6 districts to prevent unrest during the banned Awami League's anniversary.

The government has decided to deploy the Army across six districts to maintain law and order surrounding the founding anniversary of the Awami League, whose activities are currently banned.

The chosen areas for initial deployment include Dhaka, Gazipur, Narayanganj, Faridpur, Gopalganj, and Chattogram.

The troops will operate under the "In Aid to Civil Power" mandate for one week to keep the situation stable and support other law-enforcing agencies.

This move comes ahead of the June 23 anniversary events, where the government aims to prevent potential unrest.

headline_marked: UK Prime Minister [[Keir Starmer to resign]] as new leader expected by September
headline: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer to resign as new leader expected by September
summary: Starmer's decision follows plummeting popularity ratings and the rise of Andy Burnham, who is seen as a potential successor.
details: Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced on Monday that he will resign, with a new leader expected to be in place by the time parliament returns in September.
The announcement comes less than two years after Starmer won a landslide victory, promising to end political chaos in Britain.
Pressure mounted after Andy Burnham, the Mayor of Greater Manchester, won a parliamentary election on Friday, signaling a shift in support within the Labour party.
Starmer's popularity ratings have reportedly sunk to the lowest for any British leader, fueling calls for a fundamental change in leadership.
Whoever replaces Starmer will be Britain's seventh prime minister in ten years, highlighting a period of extreme political instability since the Brexit vote.
The incoming leader will inherit a precarious fiscal situation, with Britain facing the highest borrowing costs in the G7 due to high debt and slow economic growth.
Economists at Citibank have warned that a new premiership under Burnham may have few tools to deliver meaningful change given the current economic constraints.
caption:
Britain's Prime Minister Keir Starmer is stepping down. A new leader will be in place by September.

Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced on Monday that he will resign, with a new leader expected to be in place by the time parliament returns in September.

The announcement comes less than two years after Starmer won a landslide victory, promising to end political chaos in Britain.

Pressure mounted after Andy Burnham, the Mayor of Greater Manchester, won a parliamentary election on Friday, signaling a shift in support within the Labour party.

Starmer's popularity ratings have reportedly sunk to the lowest for any British leader, fueling calls for a fundamental change in leadership.

Whoever replaces Starmer will be Britain's seventh prime minister in ten years, highlighting a period of extreme political instability since the Brexit vote.

The incoming leader will inherit a precarious fiscal situation, with Britain facing the highest borrowing costs in the G7 due to high debt and slow economic growth.

Economists at Citibank have warned that a new premiership under Burnham may have few tools to deliver meaningful change given the current economic constraints.
